name: Echorer Dalna
subtitle: green jackfruit simmered in a gingery gravy until it eats like meat

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Rub your hands, knife and board with mustard oil before cutting the jackfruit. The latex is sticky and does not wash off easily.
Parboil the jackfruit first with 1/2 tsp turmeric and salt: 2 whistles in a pressure cooker, or 15 minutes in an open pan. It should take a fork with slight resistance before it meets the masala.
Drain the parboiled jackfruit thoroughly and let it steam dry for 5 minutes, or it will not brown.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadhai to smoking point, then let it cool for 30 seconds.
Fry the quartered potatoes with a pinch of turmeric and salt over medium heat for 6 minutes, until golden on all sides, and set aside.
Fry the drained jackfruit pieces in the same oil for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until they are patched with brown. Lift them out.
steps.tip: This browning is the whole point of echor. Pale jackfruit stays bland and spongy.

steps.text: Into the remaining oil add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida.
Add the ginger paste and fry for 1 minute, until it stops smelling raw.
Add the chopped tomato with the turmeric, chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, mashing as you go, until the oil separates and pools at the edges.
steps.tip: Do not shortcut this. Undercooked masala tastes chalky under the gravy.

steps.text: Return the jackfruit and potato, add the salt and sugar, and turn everything in the masala for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the gravy has thickened to coat a spoon.
Uncover, stir in the ghee and garam masala, and rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with rice or luchi.
steps.tip: Resting lets the jackfruit soak up the gravy; served straight away it tastes thin.

storage: Improves overnight and keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat on low with 3 to 4 tbsp water, as the jackfruit keeps drinking the gravy.
